findings.title: Case-sensitive email lookup and storage allows trivial bypass of blocked emails
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` without normalizing the email address (e.g., via `Email.downcase(email)`), and `BlockedEmail` does not normalize `email` before saving or validating uniqueness. On PostgreSQL (Discourse's database), `=` on `varchar` is case-sensitive, and `UsersController#create` passes `params[:email]` directly to `User.new_from_params` without downcasing it first. As a result, a blocked address like `bad@spammers.org` can be bypassed during signup simply by entering `Bad@spammers.org`.

findings.title: Validation mutates BlockedEmail match_count multiple times per signup attempt
findings.body: `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` during ActiveRecord validation, which increments `match_count` and saves the `BlockedEmail` record every time `valid?` runs. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` is called on line 168 (when `SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` is enabled) and then `user.save` runs validations again on line 172. Any caller that checks `valid?` before `save` will increment `match_count` multiple times for a single signup attempt, and read-only validation checks unexpectedly perform database writes.
